smell: 38 log sites pre-stringify the message via fmt.Sprintf instead of attaching structured attrs. CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets directs callers to prefer structured attrs so RedactHandler can inspect values; Sprintf collapses the value into the message string before the handler runs, so a cred-bearing field rendered with %v/%s is emitted verbatim.
severity_reason: Pattern is widespread (38 sites) and CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids it for redaction reasons; today none of the 38 sites flow user-supplied cred-bearing values, but the convention exists precisely so a future caller cannot accidentally smuggle one through Sprintf. Treat as design debt that has bitten the repo class before.
fix_summary: Replace `logger.Info(fmt.Sprintf("x: %s", v))` with `logger.Info("x", "key", v)` (or `tui.Info("x", tui.LF("key", v))`). For multi-value templates, expand to multiple structured attrs. Wrap the sweep in a single PR keyed off the grep `logger.(Info|Warn|Error)(fmt.Sprintf` so reviewers can verify each mechanically.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets — "Prefer structured attrs (logger.Warn("…", "err", err)) over fmt.Sprintf(…%v…) so the handler can inspect values."
must_preserve: logutil.NewRedactHandler wrap order; tui.LF constructor; CLAUDE.md ~3% comment density (don't add narrating comments to refactored sites).

smell: Four cleanup sites pass `guardErr.Error()` as the slog message rather than as a structured `err` attr. The handler sees only a free-form string, loses error-chain identity, and can't apply the cred/userinfo/Redacted() sweep that fires on attr values.
severity_reason: refuseCriticalPath today returns a fixed-format string with no creds, but the pattern is the canonical err-stringified anti-pattern flagged in seams.md §3 — observability owns the sink-side fix.
fix_summary: Rewrite as `logger.Warn("cleanup: refusing critical path", "err", guardErr)` (matches the existing idiom at services.go:139 and artifacts.go:36). One mechanical edit per site.
rule_source: seams.md §3 — sink-side err stringification is the observability axis
must_preserve: refuseCriticalPath() return-shape contract; the early-continue control flow.

smell: `tui.Warn("failed to prepend " + binDir + " to PATH: " + err.Error())` builds the full message via string concatenation, so the err's chain reaches the sink as a flat string. RedactHandler scrubs structured attr values, not the message body — any future error wrapping a cred would slip through this site.
severity_reason: Today neither site reaches a cred-bearing value (binDir/PATH are non-secret), but it's the same anti-pattern the CLAUDE.md rule was written against and lives at the preflight entry point — early-binding it now is cheaper than discovering it after a regression.
fix_summary: Replace with `tui.Warn("OKDCTL_BIN_DIR ignored", tui.LF("value", v), tui.LF("err", detail))` and `tui.Warn("failed to prepend bin dir to PATH", tui.LF("bin_dir", binDir), tui.LF("err", err))`. Two-line edit each.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/cli/root.go:120 — `tui.Error("command failed", tui.LF("err", err))` with the explicit redaction comment above it
must_preserve: preflight() ordering relative to cli.Execute; tui package-level RedactHandler wrap.

smell: `step: completed` is logged at Info level whether the step succeeded or failed. A failed fatal step is a user-visible failure — it should surface at Warn or Error so log-level filtering at the sink (e.g. `--log-level=warn`) reaches it.
severity_reason: Misclassified level — `Error` is reserved for user-visible failures (per SKILL.md). A failed orchestrator step IS user-visible (it returns up to cli.Execute and produces a non-zero exit code), so this is the textbook case for Warn (or Error if the step is fatal).
fix_summary: Branch on result: `if !result.Success { o.logger.Warn("step: failed", ...) } else { o.logger.Info("step: completed", ...) }`. If `step.IsFatal()`, escalate to Error. Keeps the structured shape; flips the level so log-filter consumers can grep.
rule_source: Google SRE — "warning means recoverable degradation; error means user-visible failure"
must_preserve: the `step: started` / `step: completed` span pair (don't drop the success-side log).

smell: `SetRunID` mutates package-level `stdoutLogger`, `stderrLogger`, and `stderrSlog` without synchronization. The doc says "Not safe for concurrent callers," but tui.Debug/Info/Warn/Error read `stderrSlog` from any goroutine after SetRunID runs — concurrent reads against the rebound pointer cross goroutine boundaries with no happens-before edge.
severity_reason: In practice SetRunID is called once at the top of executeFullDeployment before any goroutine fans out, so there's no real-world race today. But the package-level mutability is a footgun the next contributor can hit (e.g. running two phases concurrently, or a test). Documenting + sync.Once-ing the init makes the contract enforceable.
fix_summary: Either (a) wrap the three loggers in an atomic.Pointer the readers load once per call, or (b) gate SetRunID with a sync.Once so a second call panics or no-ops loudly. Both are 5-10 LOC and surface the single-init invariant in code rather than only in the doc.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §concurrency — "Every goroutine needs a stop signal or a documented leak bound"
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/root.go:73 — slog.SetDefault is called once and never mutated
Go memory model — package-level pointer mutation needs explicit sync
must_preserve: logutil.RedactHandler wrap; the .With("run_id", id) call at top of run.

smell: Cleanup summary lines use leading whitespace inside the message ("  work directory: clean") for visual indentation. Under JSON formatter the indentation becomes part of the message field; downstream log parsers can't reliably key off the message because leading spaces are syntactically significant in YAML/JSON.
severity_reason: Cosmetic discipline — only matters if `--log-format=json` consumers grep on the message. Today okdctl emits human-style text by default and `cleanup` is a single-shot CLI op, so the impact is small.
fix_summary: Move the indentation into a structured attr or use group prefix on the keys: `logger.Info("cleanup: work directory clean", "files", 0)` and let the styled charmlog formatter handle visual indentation. Alternative: wrap the printSummary calls in `slog.WithGroup("summary")` so JSON consumers get a nested structure.
rule_source: Google SRE — "key names are stable, message text is not"
must_preserve: the visual cleanup-summary affordance for TTY users.

smell: `WaitFor` logs `prefix: waiting` with `for` and `elapsed` on every poll iteration at Debug, but the start log ("waiting for X") and the ready log ("X is ready") form the span; the iteration count never appears in either bookend. Operators tailing logs can't tell from the structured record how many polls fired before ready.
severity_reason: Per SKILL §1 span-retry-boundary, span boundaries should include retry count in the after-log. Cosmetic for normal runs (single ready log is enough), real value is on the timeout error path where post-mortem analysis wants the poll budget consumed.
fix_summary: Track iteration count in the loop and append `"polls", i, "elapsed", elapsed` to the readyMsg at L81/L100 and to the timeout error at L96. Three structured attrs on existing log calls; no new sites.
rule_source: Google SRE chapter 14 — instrumenting retry loops
must_preserve: the ctx.Done()-first select shape; the existing waitMsg/readyMsg messages.

smell: `logger.Warn("cleanup warning", "err", err)` uses an unkeyed message that doesn't identify which cleanup operation failed (the parent context is `Prepare → cleanup.Execute`). Compare to the rest of the cleanup package (`cleanup: failed to stop service`, `cleanup: failed to remove package`) — this one breaks the established `cleanup: <verb> <object>` key convention.
severity_reason: Field/message-stability axis. The message reads ambiguously in a multi-cluster log stream — switching to `cleanup: pre-deploy artifact removal incomplete` makes the key consistent with siblings and the `phase` attribute identifiable.
fix_summary: `p.logger.Warn("cleanup: pre-deploy artifact removal incomplete", "phase", "prepare", "err", err)`. Adds a `phase` attr matching orchestrator's `step` key style.
must_preserve: the soft-fail behavior (cleanup error must not break Prepare).

smell: On terraform apply failure, the warn log carries the user-facing recovery hint ("run 'okdctl destroy'") but does NOT carry the apply error itself as an attr. The error then surfaces only via `fmt.Errorf(... %w ...)` two lines later — the slog record has no `err` field, so log-aggregation can't filter by error class.
severity_reason: Span-boundary discipline: `terraform: applying...` (L152) starts the span, this is the failure-side close. Without `"err", applyErr` on the warn, the structured record is missing the most actionable attr — what went wrong.
fix_summary: `p.logger.Warn("terraform: apply failed; run 'okdctl destroy' to clean up partial infrastructure", "err", applyErr)`. Single-attr addition; recovery hint stays in the message so TTY users still see it.
rule_source: audit-observability/SKILL.md §1 span-retry-boundary — "include retry/failure context in the after-log"
must_preserve: the user-facing recovery hint text; the fmt.Errorf wrap (errors path).

smell: `tui.Error(fmt.Sprintf("doctor: %d failing check(s), %d warning(s): fix before deploying", fails, warns))` uses Error-level for an advisory exit summary. SKILL.md §1 reserves Error for user-visible *failures*; doctor is a read-only diagnostic, the surfaced failure is in the per-check loop above this — this line is the recap.
evidence:
// internal/cli/doctor.go:103
tui.Error(fmt.Sprintf("doctor: %d failing check(s), %d warning(s): fix before deploying", fails, warns))
severity_reason: The per-check failures already log as Error inside checkRow (printed by the styled formatter). This recap is informational. Demoting to Warn keeps the styling distinct from the per-check level without claiming a new failure event.
fix_summary: Either drop to `tui.Warn(...)` (recap is not a new failure) or, more idiomatic, keep Error but make it structured: `tui.Error("doctor: failing checks block deploy", tui.LF("failing", fails), tui.LF("warnings", warns))` so log-aggregation can plot the count.
must_preserve: the non-zero exit-code path doctor takes when fails > 0.
